claim: B2024-010 Feb 2024 arrested: total 621 vs short briefings 648
evidence: The February statement gives 621 "others" apprehended and lists 359 oil-theft arrests separately, so the total excludes oil-theft arrests. Of the parts, B2024-008 (264) is stated as "including 104 perpetrators of oil theft"; excluding them gives 160, and the parts inside February sum to 140 + 160 + 244 = 544, below 621. The gap is a definitional mismatch, not a DHQ inconsistency.

claim: B2024-023 May 2024 rescued: total 563 vs three weekly totals 599
evidence: Weekly rescues 140 (4-10 May), 253 (10-16 May) and 206 (18-24 May) are each stated as one week by two or more independent copies; together they exceed the May total of 563, announced on 30 May, by 36, with 1-3 and 25-31 May not yet counted. Caveat: Channels TV describes the 253 as "the last two weeks"; if so, it overlaps the 4-10 May week and the gap disappears. Development year (2024).

claim: B2024-037 Aug 2024 neutralised: total 1,166 vs parts 426, residual 575.6 per missing week (2.01 x the largest weekly figure)
evidence: The monthly total (1,166, announced 29 August 2024) and the three weekly parts (108, 147, 171) are confirmed in the texts. 9 of the 29 days to the announcement are uncovered (1.29 weeks), implying 575.6 neutralised per missing week, 2.01 times the largest 2024 weekly figure (286); the result is the same in the grade-2-only rerun, and the row is grade 2 after the single grading rule. Reproduces the pilot result C065. Announced before the month ended. Development year (2024).

claim: B2024-057 annual 2024 neutralised: 10,937 vs year-to-date 8,034 plus December weeklies 541
verdict: upheld; holds on grade 2 figures alone
evidence: The year-to-date total (8,034, announced 5 December 2024, "from January to December" / "in 11 months") and the annual total (10,937, announced 31 December 2024) are both grade 2 under the single grading rule. In the grade-2-only rerun (outputs/audit_v1.0/sensitivity/grade2_residual.csv) the known parts are 8,034 plus the grade-2 weekly figures for B2024-055 (212) and B2024-056 (148), 8,394 in all; 12 of the 26 days from 6 to 31 December are uncovered (1.71 weeks), so the remaining 2,543 imply 1,483.4 neutralised per missing week, 5.19 times the largest weekly figure DHQ reported in 2024 (286, B2024-009). Arrested (12,538 against 12,399) and rescued (7,063 against 6,980) line up with the same parts, so the jump is specific to the neutralised count. If 8,034 was meant as a full-year figure, the two annual figures conflict outright. Development year (2024).

claim: Period end: 9 totals announced before the period they name had ended
evidence: Monthly totals for May 2024, August 2024, January, February and May 2026, quarterly totals for Q2 and Q3 2024, and annual totals for 2021 and 2023 were announced 1 to 5 days before the stated period ended (7 at grade 2). The figures therefore cannot cover the final days of the period they are labelled with.

claim: B2024-033 July 2024 (coverage variant): totals 572 / 790 / 479 against briefings dated in July 595 / 810 / 510
evidence: The coverage variant counts parts by briefing date, so it includes B2024-029 (inferred period 29 June to 5 July), two of whose seven days fall in June. Its June share (about 51 neutralised, 75 arrested and 45 rescued on a pro-rata basis) exceeds each excess (23, 20 and 31), and 26 to 31 July is covered by no weekly part. The period rule (month_weeks) does not report a gap for July. Development year (2024).
